conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve had bad stomach pain for about two days now, and a lot of diarrhea. It feels like one of my usual Crohn’s flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I see you have a history of Crohn’s disease and several past surgeries. Is this pain similar to previous flares?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly like before. The diarrhea slowed this morning, but now the pain is more crampy. That usually happens when things slow down—my anatomy makes it hard to pass stool during flares.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You mentioned manual disimpaction doesn’t help much?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right. It never works for me. Usually, IV fluids help it pass on its own after a day or so.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We’ve reviewed your CT scan from tonight. There’s some fecal loading in the distal ileum and mild inflammation, but actually, it looks improved compared to your last scan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good, I guess. But why the pain then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The pain is likely from the flare itself—your bowel is inflamed and the backed-up stool is stretching the area. But no obstruction, which is reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. I didn’t take the IV steroid they offered in the ER—was that a mistake?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not at all. We’re going to start you on 40 mg of oral prednisone daily. That’s a higher dose than you were on, and it should help calm the flare.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was only on 5 mg before. Is that safe?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, for a short time. Your GI doctor will taper it down later. We’re also giving IV fluids to rehydrate you and help the stool move through.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been feeling a bit weak. My labs okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your kidney function was a bit off when you arrived—creatinine was 1.5, up from your baseline of 1.0. But that’s likely from dehydration. We’re fixing that with fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the acidosis I saw on the board? What’s that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. Your bicarbonate was low at 13, but no anion gap and lactate was normal. It’s a metabolic acidosis from losing bicarbonate in diarrhea. We’re replacing it with IV fluids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not long-term. It should correct as you rehydrate. We’ll check your labs again in the morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I just reviewed your morning labs. Your creatinine is already down to 1.3, and bicarbonate is up to 18. That’s improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. My pain is also a lot better. I had a small bowel movement this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent. We’re going to advance your diet to regular food today—lunch and dinner—if you can tolerate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I stop the IV fluids then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep them going for now, but if you eat and drink well, we can remove them later today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The stool test came back—no C. diff, no parasites, no salmonella or shigella. Infection is unlikely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s definitely Crohn’s?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, everything points to a flare. We’re stopping the Cipro since we don’t think it’s an infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did an ultrasound to check for a hernia, since your pain is in the lower right. Good news—it’s negative. No hernia.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I was worried about that. Thanks for checking.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. Your labs are almost back to normal—creatinine is 0.9, bicarbonate is 23. You’re euvolemic and tolerating food well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I can go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re discharging you today. You’ll continue the 40 mg prednisone daily until you see your GI doctor—they’ll taper it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about pain? I might need something for a few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re prescribing a short course of oxycodone for breakthrough pain—take as needed, up to four times a day, but only if necessary.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll keep taking omeprazole, B12 injections, and Tysabri. Loperamide only if diarrhea returns. And quetiapine at night if you need help sleeping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will the urine and stool cultures still be checked?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, they’re still pending, but we’ll follow up. If anything comes back positive, someone will contact you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks, Doctor. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Keep drinking fluids, take your meds, and follow up with GI soon. We’ll get you set up to go home in a few hours.
